Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The umpires and the players have made their way out in the middle. Aiden Markram and Dean Elgar are the openers for South Africa. Kemar Roach comes to bowl. Here we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

South Africa have put on a brilliant team display with the ball and will come out to bat once again feeling pretty comfortable. Everyone in the bowling lineup picked up at least a wicket and it was Gerald Coetzee who was the best of the bunch. They could have had an even bigger lead but they will take it. They will now look to go into Day 3 with no loss. Stay tuned as the South African second innings is up next.

West Indies were under the pump all throughout their innings and the lack of big partnerships has cost them dearly. They will be thankful to Jason Holder who played a sublime knock and was well-supported by Gudakesh Motie at the end. They stitched a partnership of 58 runs at the end and reduced the lead to 69 runs.

That is it, West Indies have been bundled out for 251 runs and South Africa has a lead of 69 runs in the bag. They will come out in their second innings and look to stretch it over the 350-run mark at the very least but it will be interesting to see how the visitors respond with the ball.

OUT! TAKEN! Slightly shorter and on off, Gudakesh Motie looks to pull it but gets a leading edge as the ball lobs towards covers. Temba Bavuma settles under it and takes a dolly. West Indies end their inning at 251 runs and they now trail by 69 runs!
Commentary.Howout: c Temba Bavuma b Simon Harmer

We are back for the final session of the day. The umpires and the players have made their way out in the middle. Joshua Da Silva and Jason Holder will resume their innings. Simon Harmer comes to bowl. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

South Africa will be happy as well. They have kept West Indies on the back foot but to have the upper hand they have to keep taking the wickets. Kagiso Rabada bowled brilliantly in this session and so did Keshav Maharaj who will have a go again in the final session. We have seen how the final session of Day 1 produce maximum wickets, will it be the same this time around? Will find out soon.

A much needed partnership in the making for the Windies as they were in tatters at the start. They lost two wickets in this session but in the last hour or so, Joshua Da Silva and Jason Holder have batted brilliantly. We saw Holder getting a bit aggressive as spinners are getting some purchases on it. West Indies still have a long way to go but will love these two to bat for a long period.
